module.title: Hash Maps & Stacks
module.subtitle: Fast frequency counting with dicts and LIFO undo history with stacks
lesson_points: A dictionary (hash map) jumps straight to counts[key] in constant time instead of scanning a whole list.
Use counts.get(key, 0) + 1 to safely count items even on the very first time you see a key.
A stack is a list where you push onto the top with .append() and remove the newest item with .pop() (Last-In, First-Out).
module.example_code:
events = ["hit", "heal", "hit", "hit"]
counts = {}
undo_stack = []

for ev in events:
    counts[ev] = counts.get(ev, 0) + 1
    undo_stack.append(ev)

last = undo_stack.pop()
print("Counts:", counts, "Undid:", last)

quizzes.title: Stack Pop Order (LIFO)
quizzes.prompt: What does stack.pop() return after pushing 'a', 'b', 'c'?
quizzes.code:
stack = []
for item in ["a", "b", "c"]:
    stack.append(item)
print(stack.pop())
quizzes.explanation: Stacks are Last-In, First-Out (LIFO): 'c' was appended last, so .pop() removes and returns 'c'.

quizzes.title: Spot the KeyError Trap
quizzes.prompt: Click the line that crashes with KeyError on the first unseen word.
quizzes.explanation: Line 3 tries to read counts['go'] before it exists. Use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1 instead.

quizzes.title: Safe Undo Guard
quizzes.prompt: Order these blocks so popping from history never crashes when empty.
quizzes.explanation: Check 'if not history: return None' before calling .pop().
